title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
This is an operational-envelope failure rather than a perception or prediction error. The vehicles performed as designed in ordinary traffic, then ran out of energy in conditions the service had not provisioned for: sustained standstill congestion, unusually high traveler volume, and road closures the company described as unexpected. The failure surfaced at the fleet level, in energy management and dispatch, not in the driving policy itself. A vehicle that cannot complete or exit a trip because its battery is drained is a stranded vehicle regardless of how well it drove to that point.

Catching this would have required treating prolonged low-speed congestion as a known operating condition rather than an edge case. That means an energy budget that accounts for hours of near-zero progress, monitoring of state of charge against a reserve threshold that triggers a reroute or a hold, and timely ingestion of road closure information so vehicles are not routed into a jam they cannot leave. The reported fire after a vehicle drove over ignited fireworks points to a separate question about how the system responds to debris and hazards in the roadway, which is a detection problem rather than an energy one.

What is not established: the account of a vehicle continuing to drive while fireworks went off nearby comes from one passenger and is not a finding. The cause of the fire is not established as a fault in the vehicle. No injuries occurred, and the mayor's office announced discussions about future traffic management, which is not a regulatory action or a determination of fault.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Several Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets after their batteries depleted during severe traffic congestion following Fourth of July fireworks celebrations near the Golden Gate Bridge. Video footage showed at least a dozen stationary Waymo vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up on streets, with some requiring towing. The company attributed the incident to major traffic disruptions, high traveler volume, and unexpected road closures. Additionally, one Waymo vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks that someone had ignited in the roadway, though no injuries occurred.

The gridlock caused significant frustration among stranded motorists, with some spending nearly two hours in standstill traffic. One passenger reported the autonomous vehicle continued driving despite fireworks being set off nearby. Mayor Daniel Lurie's office announced plans to hold discussions with public and private partners about improving traffic management for future events. Waymo stated it is evaluating ways to strengthen its vehicles' resilience during major traffic disruptions. The incident marks another challenge for the autonomous vehicle service in San Francisco, following a similar issue during a December power outage.
